options.text: Earth supports life because linked surface conditions such as air, liquid water, soil, shelter, and food occur together in a thin living layer.
Earth supports life because frozen water alone is enough, even with no liquid water, air, or soil.
Life appears first on the ice-covered moon, and that appearance then brings air, soil, and liquid water.
Earth supports life only because its deep rocky core is the only place living things can grow.

stem:
Nidhi compares Earth with an ice-covered moon that has frozen water but no liquid water, no breathable air near the surface, no soil, and no thin living surface layer with linked resources.

Which claim best explains why Earth can support life as we know it?

teacher.key_rationale: Earth supports life through linked near-surface conditions together, not one feature alone, not life creating those conditions afterward, and not only a deep core habitat.
